names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 5 august, «Sfântul Mucenic Evsignie», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 5 Αυγούστου, «Άγιος Ευσίγνιος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue’s first heading for the Julian 5 August, „Св. муч. Евсигније.“ — Св. муч. left off, which §5 maps to `martyr`. The heading gives no city and no by-name, so the bare forename is the whole of the form; Antioch is in the body, where a name form may not reach. `.tmp/sr-foldpred.mjs` reports it folds with nothing.

death.note: doxologia.ro gives no year, only the reign and his age: it has him serving sixty years from Diocletian and Maximian to Constantius the son of Constantine, and then «Iar Iulian, nesuferind să audă aceste cuvinte, a poruncit să-i taie capul ostașului lui Hristos. Astfel s-a sfârșit Sfântul Evsignie pentru Hristos, ca un mucenic, având vârsta de 110 ani». The interval is Julian's reign, 361–363.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 5 august — «Sfântul Mucenic Evsignie»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 5ης Αυγούστου — «Άγιος Ευσίγνιος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 5 Αυγούστου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and it is the same man: born at Antioch, a soldier for sixty whole years, enlisted under Constans Chlorus the father of Constantine the Great, and beheaded under Julian the Apostate. saint.gr is more definite about the year than doxologia was — its head line reads «Αγιος Ευσιγνιος (252 - 362)» and its last sentence «Έτσι ο Ευσίγνιος έλαβε τον τίμιο θάνατο του μαρτυρίου με αποκεφαλισμό το 362 μ.Χ.» — and it gives his age as 110, «κάποιος γέροντας στρατιώτης 110 χρονών». The folder's `dates` are left as the Romanian pass set them, `under Julian`, 361 to 363, which the Greek year falls inside; the Greek figures are recorded in the life instead, and whether the firmer 252 and 362 should replace that interval is a question for the writer and is in the report. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page. The page prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both of which name him, and both are taken.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 18.08.2026 (5. август ст. ст.) — „Св. муч. Евсигније.“

attestations.note: The day’s first of four entries, and the Romanian and Greek both keep him on this same 5/8. His row was `undocumented`. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND THE BOOK’S FLAT YEAR SITS INSIDE THE INTERVAL THE FOLDER ALREADY HELD.** „Огорчени Јулијан нареди те му главу одсекоше. Пострада Евсигније у дубокој старости 362 год. и пресели се у царство небеско.“ — the embittered Julian gave the order and they cut off his head; Eusignius suffered in deep old age in 362 and passed over to the heavenly kingdom. The folder holds `death` 361–363, display «under Julian», basis traditional, which was written from the reign and not from a year; **362 is the middle of it**, so narrowing the interval onto the new reading would throw away what the other two books gave and gain nothing a reader can check. Nothing is written, and the year is in the row note and in the life as the book’s. **A RELATION STATED, AND THE ONE IDENTIFICATION IN THIS BLOCK THAT RESTS ON A NAME AND AN EPITHET RATHER THAN ON A DAY.** „Присуствовао мучењу св. муч. Василиска (22. маја), видео мноштво ангела и самог Господа Исуса, како од ангела прима душу овог светог мученика.“ — he was present at the martyrdom of the holy martyr Basiliscus, the entry adding the day 22 May in brackets, and saw a multitude of angels and the Lord Jesus himself receiving that martyr’s soul from the angels. Being present at a man’s passion is the same act the Julian 7 August relates Asterius to Marinus by, so the row is written both ways — **but which Basiliscus is a reading, and it is made here on the name plus one stored form.** The corpus holds two: `basiliscus-the-elder`, a Greek «Άγιος Βασιλίσκος ο γέρων» of 29 July, who is an elder and not a martyr of a passion anybody attended; and `basiliscus-of-amasea`, a martyr whose **Russian stored form is «Василиск Команский»**, Basiliscus of Comana, who is the Basiliscus of Comana the Slavonic books keep on 22 May. **No folder in this corpus carries any feast on 22/5**, so the cross-reference points at a day nothing is kept on, and the match is therefore not on the day. It is written because the epithet names the right man and the only other candidate is excluded by his own rank and day, and it is named in the findings as the block’s one name-and-epithet identification so that the author can strike it in one line if it is wrong. `constantine-the-great` was `related` here already and in both directions: „Војевао при цару Константину и видео крст, који се јавио Константину.“ has him campaign under Constantine and see the cross that appeared to him, and „Цар позва Евсигнија на суд, но он изобличи цара страшно за одступништво од вере и укори га светлим примером великог Константина.“ has him rebuke Julian by Constantine’s bright example, so nothing is added there. **`types` UNTOUCHED.** Св. муч. is `martyr` and the folder has it; војник, a soldier, is in the body and not in the heading and is refused as a body word under the Julian 27 June ruling — and `soldier` is on the folder already from the other two books, so the refusal costs nothing here. Maximian, Julian the Apostate and the sons of Constantine are emperors named to place a life and take no row; the two men who asked him to judge their quarrel are unnamed. No `locations`: Antioch is named in a clause. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person.

hymns.text: Mucenicul Tău, Doamne, Evsignie, întru nevoinţa sa, cununa nestricăciunii a dobândit de la Tine, Dumnezeul nostru; că având puterea Ta, pe chinuitori a învins; zdrobit-a şi ale demonilor neputincioase îndrăzniri. Pentru rugăciunile lui, mântuieşte sufletele noastre, Hristoase Dumnezeule.

english.text: Your martyr Eusignius, O Lord, in his struggle received from You, our God, the crown of incorruption; for having Your strength he overthrew the torturers and broke the powerless insolence of the demons. At his prayers, Christ God, save our souls.

hymns.text: Ὡς ἔμπλεως πίστεως, τῆς πρὸς Χριστὸν εὐσεβῶς, νεάζον τὸ φρόνημα, ἔσχες ἐν γήρᾳ καλῶς, Εὐσίγνιε ἔνδοξε, ὅθεν ὁμολογήσας, τὸν Ὑπέρθεον Λόγον, ἤλεγξας θαρσαλέως, Παραβάτου τὸ θράσος, ἐντεῦθεν μετὰ Μαρτύρων, ὡς Μάρτυς δεδόξασαι.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον (Κατέβασμα), Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιος Ευσίγνιος», and it names him, «Εὐσίγνιε ἔνδοξε»

english.text: Filled full of faith towards Christ in piety, you kept a young mind nobly in your old age, glorious Eusignios; and so, confessing the Word who is above God's own naming, you rebuked with courage the insolence of the Apostate, and from that hour you are glorified with the martyrs, a martyr yourself.

hymns.text: Ὡς εὐσεβείας μάρτυρα, καὶ ἀληθῆ θεόφρονα, ἡ Ἐκκλησία γεραίρει δοξάζουσα, τοὺς θείους ἄθλους σήμερον, τοῦ σοφοῦ Εὐσιγνίου, ἀκαταπαύστως βοώσα, Ταὶς αὐτοῦ ἰκεσίαις, τοὺς δούλους σου συντήρησον Πολυέλεε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος πλ. δ’, Ὡς ἀπαρχᾶς — the second hymn on the page of «Άγιος Ευσίγνιος», and it too names him, «τοῦ σοφοῦ Εὐσιγνίου»

english.text: As a martyr of piety and a true man of God's mind, the Church honours and glorifies today the divine contests of the wise Eusignios, crying out unceasingly: by his entreaties keep Your servants, O Lord rich in mercy.
